summary.intent: Run a quality cleanup pass (/simplify) on session changes, then execute the GSD secure-phase workflow to verify threat mitigations for Phase 42 (api-unpin-integrity) and produce a SECURITY.md artifact.
summary.outcome: The simplify review found no issues — the changed code was already clean. The security auditor verified all 22 mitigate-disposition threats as CLOSED with file:line evidence; Phase 42 SECURITY.md was written to `.planning/phases/42-api-unpin-integrity/42-SECURITY.md` and committed.

repo: Phase 42 (api-unpin-integrity) spans 8 sub-plans and 8 summaries, each carrying a <threat_model> block — register_authored_at_plan_time is true for this phase.
Phase summaries use '## Threat Surface Scan' (not '## Threat Flags') as the heading for security-relevant observations.
The repo root SECURITY.md (127 lines, introduced in #482) is a security-disclosure policy unrelated to the GSD phase artifact — the two must not be conflated.
The fetch-timeout pattern is duplicated in at least 4 places: tee, delegated-routing, migration processor, and the new api-unpin code — a known consolidation opportunity not yet acted on.
The codebase convention in scripts is: every terminal path calls dataSource.destroy() + process.exit(N) independently, so apparent duplication is intentional.
NODE_ENV inline checks (rather than a shared isProduction helper) match the established codebase convention.

code.finding: Phase SECURITY.md created in State B (no prior SECURITY.md, PLAN + SUMMARY existed). Contains 28 threats: 22 mitigate (all CLOSED), 6 accept, 1 supply-chain accept.

workflow: The gsd-security-auditor subagent had Write access and incorrectly wrote to the repo root SECURITY.md instead of the phase directory — the clobber had to be detected and reverted via git checkout before writing the correct artifact.
When dispatching 4 parallel agents via the Agent tool, all 4 must be sent in a single message; sending 2 then 2 in a follow-up message is a recoverable but avoidable inefficiency.

The short-circuit rule (threats_open: 0 AND register_authored_at_plan_time: true → skip to Step 6) did NOT apply here because accepted-risk threats are not open threats — the auditor still ran to verify the 22 mitigate threats, which is correct.
The GSD commit helper (gsd_run query commit) can report false negatives; verifying with git log afterward is the reliable check.

friction: The gsd-security-auditor subagent clobbered the repo-root SECURITY.md (an unrelated security-disclosure policy from #482) by appending 54 lines to it — required detection, revert, and then writing the correct phase artifact manually.
Only 2 of 4 parallel simplify agents were launched in the first Agent tool message; the other 2 were dispatched in a second message, breaking the intended single-message concurrency.
open_items: Extract a shared fetchWithTimeout utility — the pattern now exists in 4 files (tee, delegated-routing, migration, api-unpin); deferred because it spans files well outside this diff.
Consider promoting suppressCrossUserAudit boolean to an intent enum once there are more than 2 callers — deferred as over-engineering at current N=2.
Audit subagent (gsd-security-auditor) needs a constraint or path guard to prevent it from writing to the repo root SECURITY.md — it should only be permitted to write inside the phase directory.
